text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from typical childhood absence seizures).

*Note: While the 3–4 minute duration is unusually long for typical absence seizures and suggests a focal onset or status epilepticus, the core clinical picture of staring, unresponsiveness, post-ictal confusion, and an oral aura ("muddy taste") in a 7-year-old strongly points to an epileptic etiology. Given the patient is currently presenting with "episodes" that just occurred, I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the history provided, as further questioning would consume my remaining queries without altering the immediate clinical urgency.*
